neighbours.label: Covering or obstructing an opening or passage (curtains over windows, a stent or plaque in an artery, something packed into a snowbank), firing on the connective that introduces the covering/blockage, as a predictor of 'block/obstruct' content
fire: The bedroom windows were covered with thick blankets to keep out the light.
Over the years a buildup of calcium narrowed the pipe until water barely flowed.
Surgeons inserted a balloon into the blocked vessel to widen it again.
During the blackout, every window in the street was screened by dark paper.
Hang heavy curtains over the glass door to stop the afternoon glare.
A clot lodged in the coronary artery and cut off blood flow to the heart.
The cave entrance was sealed with boulders after the landslide.
Leaves and mud clogged the drain, so the yard flooded after the storm.
quiet: The bedroom windows were opened wide to let in the morning light.
Over the years the pipe was replaced twice as the house was extended.
Surgeons examined the healthy vessel and found it in good condition.
During the festival, every window in the street displayed colorful flags.
Slide open the glass door to enjoy the view of the garden.
Regular exercise keeps the coronary arteries healthy and flexible.
The cave entrance was wide enough for three people to walk in side by side.
The drain ran freely, so the yard stayed dry after the storm.
